caveats: E2 is an approximate held-out split: landmark positions still come from the full model (only the map images/observations and descriptors are map-only). A fully clean variant would rebuild the map with the mapper on even frames only (E3).
Queries are cam1 only; the example takes a single --camera-id.
A handful of queries (5/625) localize to a wrong pose (max ~9-14 m / 86-161 deg), presumably perceptual aliasing in the corridor; median/p95 are unaffected.
The reference pose is the mapper's own pose, so this measures recovery of the map pose, not absolute GT accuracy.

map.descriptors: SIFT 128-dim uint8 from the COLMAP DB, one representative map observation per landmark

queries.reference: the image's world_to_camera in the full tier-2500 mapper model (GT-free self-consistency)
queries.selection: cam1 images of odd frames of tier-2500 (held out under --held-out-parity even)

reproduction: export landmark descriptors + even/odd split, build examples/localize_openloris_map, run scripts/eval_openloris_map_relocalization.py; see docs/openloris_map_relocalization_plan.md
summary: Map-based single-image relocalization against a map built by the native COLMAP port (examples/colmap_incremental_mapper) works: 625/625 cam1 odd-frame queries localize with median ~3 mm / 0.07 deg error vs the mapper's own pose, 99.2% within 0.5 m / 2 deg, both when the map contains the query frame (E1 self) and when it does not (E2 held-out even-frame map).
